written.myAnswer: Permanent magnets are used in compasses and loudspeakers. Electromagnets are used in electric bells, relays, circuit breakers, telephone receivers and magnetic cranes.
A current-carrying long coil (solenoid) produces a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet.

A circuit breaker is a safety device that breaks a circuit when the current exceeds a safe limit. The current passes through a coil and copper-strip contact. Excessive current makes the coil’s electromagnet strong enough to attract the iron armature away from the contact, opening the circuit.

```text
Copper-strip contact ── coil (electromagnet) ── circuit
           ↑                    │
           └── armature attracted when current is excessive
                (moves away from contact to break circuit)
```
